extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working at the intersection of NLP / multimodal AI and patent analysis (including patent offices and patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive survey of NLP and multimodal-AI methods for patent-related tasks (classification, retrieval, quality analysis, and generation), summarizing datasets, methods, evaluation metrics, challenges, and future directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent classification evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation measures for patent classification are accuracy, precision, recall, and the f1 score on the CPC or IPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used at different hierarchy levels (Section, Class, Subclass, Group, Subgroup). Results should be reported per hierarchy level because a single patent can have multiple labels; some works also report top-3 accuracy. Comparisons must account for multi-label and hierarchical nature of the task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-label, hierarchical modelling for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent classification is multi-label and hierarchical (IPC/CPC): a single patent can be assigned multiple codes across a hierarchy (sections → classes → subclasses → groups → subgroups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models must capture dependencies between broad and fine-grained categories and handle multi-label outputs. Techniques include fixed-hierarchy vectors, hierarchical loss/designs, and section-aware inputs. Failure to model hierarchy leads to poorer subclass-level performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section-aware document representation (section selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent documents have multiple sections (title, abstract, description, claims); different sections contain different information useful to different tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For classification/retrieval/generation, select or weight relevant sections (e.g., claims for classification) or design multi-section models (MSABERT, multi-input architectures). Ignoring section structure or using only full-text naively can reduce performance and increase computational cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent retrieval evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent retrieval systems compute similarity scores (e.g., cosine) between a query patent and candidate patents and return top-k results; evaluation metrics reported include precision, recall, F1, mean average precision (mAP), and sometimes accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because retrieval is used to assess novelty/prior art, metrics like mAP are common for ranking quality. Retrieval methods must handle synonyms, varied phrasings, and merge results from multiple databases. Report dataset(s) used and whether retrieval is text-only, image-only, or multimodal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query construction quality for prior-art search
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructing effective search queries (alternate search terms, related words, synonyms) is critical because query quality directly impacts retrieval relevance and novelty assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automating query expansion or generation is an open challenge. Systems that cannot propose diverse search terms will miss relevant prior art; techniques like query expansion and semantic similarity help improve recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent image retrieval and image-specific challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent image retrieval must handle patent drawings (typically black-and-white sketches with numbers) and retrieve relevant patents from an image or a multimodal query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image methods (CNNs, ResNet, Vision Transformers, deep metric learning) should account for non-natural image characteristics. Evaluation commonly uses mAP. Models like CLIP, BLIP-2 and contrastive/metric losses (InfoNCE, ArcFace) have been effective; evaluate on image-specific patent datasets (DeepPatent, DeepPatent2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal alignment and fusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are multimodal (text + images); systems should align representations derived from textual descriptions with those from technical images to enable joint retrieval, generation, or classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fusion strategies include late fusion (separate encoders), contrastive alignment (dual encoders + InfoNCE), and joint encoder approaches. Because patent images are more technical than natural images, specialized visual encoders or fine-tuning on patent drawings is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality indicators as evaluation targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonly used measures for patent quality/value include forward citations, backward citations, number of claims, grant lag, patent family size, remaining lifetime, maintenance period, and investor reaction; composite indices such as OECD indices are also used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indicators are used as prediction targets in patent-quality models (regression/classification). However, their relation to actual monetary value is ambiguous; forward citations are most directly associated with value but weighting of indices is unclear. Researchers should state which proxy they use and justify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of universally accepted gold-standard for patent value
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no universally accepted 'gold standard' metric for patent quality/value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of metric ambiguity, experiments should report multiple indicators, discuss limitations, and avoid claiming definitive monetary valuation solely from citation-based proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of domain-adaptive pretraining and fine-tuning of PLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tuning pretrained language models (BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet) on patent datasets or using domain-adaptive masking (e.g., SciBERT-style pretraining) improves classification and retrieval performance in the patent domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent text differs from scientific or news text; fine-tune on large patent corpora (USPTO-2M, USPTO-3M, etc.) or pretrain/adapt masking strategies to capture technical language. Report dataset and fine-tuning details because they materially affect results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and comparison limitations due to dataset and hierarchy differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons across methods are limited by differences in datasets, dataset subsets, class hierarchies, and evaluation metrics used in different studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting results, specify dataset versions, hierarchy levels, and evaluation protocols. Encourage standard benchmarks and reproducible splits to enable fair comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for patent generation are insufficient (BLEU/ROUGE limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic textual metrics like BLEU and ROUGE are insufficient to assess factual accuracy, novelty, or legal correctness of generated patent text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement automatic metrics with retrieval-based evaluation (check consistency with prior art), domain-specific factuality checks, human/expert review, and legal/novelty criteria. Report multiple evaluation modes and their limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval-augmented evaluation and generation (RAG) for grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrieval-augmented generation and retrieval-based evaluation help ground generated patent content in existing prior art, improving factual accuracy and reducing infringement risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RAG at generation time or as an evaluation step: compare generated content against retrieved patents to check novelty and avoid hallucinated or infringing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-in-the-loop and expert feedback (RLHF) for legal robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Human oversight and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) with patent experts (attorneys/reviewers) are necessary to align generated patent outputs with drafting goals (novelty, clarity, consistency with prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reward functions that encode drafting preferences (e.g., favourable claim length, inclusion of limiting terms). Use structured expert ratings on novelty, clarity, and consistency to train or fine-tune models; report the human evaluation protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding hallucination and ensuring factual/legal correctness in generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative models (LLMs) can hallucinate, produce repetitive/monotonous text, or invent unsupported technical features; this risks inaccurate or legally problematic patent drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation strategies include RAG, RLHF, retrieval-based checks, and mandatory human revision. Do not treat automated outputs as legally ready; always require patent-expert review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designing reward functions for claim drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Custom reward functions (for RLHF) can be constructed to prefer claim attributes (e.g., claim length up to a defined length, inclusion of limiting terms) that improve chances of patent approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe reward components and their rationale. Rewarding limiting terms and appropriate length can help reduce overbroad or vague claims, but trade-offs with completeness must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling dependency between patent parts for generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent generation benefits from modeling dependencies among parts (e.g., using abstract/claims to generate specification or using claim+drawing to produce specification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generative tasks can be formulated as part-to-part generation (Claim → Specification, Claim+Drawing → Specification). Use appropriate conditioning inputs and multimodal encoders when images are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational cost and scalability for long patent texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Models that handle multi-section long texts (e.g., MSABERT) can be computationally costly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance model capacity and cost; when using long-document or multi-section models, report computational requirements and consider efficient encoders or section-selection heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contrastive and deep metric learning for robust representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrastive losses (InfoNCE) and angular margin losses (ArcFace) and deep metric learning frameworks improve representation quality, especially for multimodal retrieval and tail classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply distribution-aware contrastive losses to preserve class/category information and improve robustness for rare classes. Report training loss formulations and sampling strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building and using knowledge graphs / citation networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing patents as nodes in knowledge/citation graphs (with edges for citations, metadata, semantic similarity) supports citation analysis, prior-art search, and valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate metadata, semantic similarity, inventor networks and citations into a knowledge graph to improve retrieval and quality assessment. Describe graph construction and embedding methods (TransE, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-jurisdictional retrieval and generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-jurisdictional patent retrieval (e.g., USPTO ↔ EPO) introduces challenges from differences in legal terminology, language, classification codes, and document formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design retrieval systems tolerant to terminology and formatting differences and evaluate cross-corpus generalization. Report multi-jurisdiction performance where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting dataset details and task formulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly report dataset sizes, formats, datatypes (text/image), and intended tasks (classification, retrieval, generation) because these materially affect reproducibility and comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard datasets when possible (USPTO-2M, USPTO-3M, BigPatent, DeepPatent, DeepPatent2, PatentMatch, HUPD, IMPACT) and provide data splits, preprocessing, and hierarchy-level choices in publications.
